title: Short notation
goal: How keymux, lyk and this site write a stroke for people: a group of keys whose sound is known as the standard letter for it, every other stroke as raw keys; and how both forms are read back.

blocks.x: **A group of keys is written as one symbol only where its split is known.** An outline lyk wrote from a word's sounds is known: each chord that wrote one sound is written as that sound's symbol, vowels and the star as below: [[flight|TPHRAOEUT]] shows as `FLĪT`, [[night|TPHAOEUT]] as `NĪT`, [[wish|WEURB]] as `WIŠ`, [[tax|TABGS]] as `TAX`. Every other stroke is shown raw, a key each, because a guess at its split could be wrong: [[enemy|TPHAEPL]] (a brief) stays `TPHAEPL`, [[narrates|TPHRA*EUTS]] and [[nature|TPHRAEUFP]] (short forms whose `TPHR` is N and R, not FL) stay raw. Dictionary files and every page source stay raw. Input takes both forms.

blocks.x: One character where a standard one exists (dictionary respelling, IPA or established spelling), else the usual dictionary respelling in capitals. A group is written in its hand's colour as one piece. The **source** column says where each symbol comes from; *base* chords are the `[onset]` and `[coda]` of `rules/plover.toml`, *cluster* chords are fixed in `src/notation.rs` (`CLUSTERS`), *measured* ones are chosen by `build` (see [how they were chosen](#/ref/notation/how-the-groups-were-chosen)); the counts are strokes lyk wrote from sounds.

blocks.x: Every other key is its own letter. A run of keys is read from its lowest key: the group with the most keys that starts there, whose keys are all down and with no other key still to write inside its span (`SR` `V` is never read inside `STR`), else the key's own letter. `#` strokes are `#` and letters (`#TR-RL`), never Plover's digits.

A vowel chord is always one sound in lyk (one stroke, one syllable, one vowel), so no outline is an exception for its vowel keys: the mark names the chord. **The star follows the mark**: `AO*EU` is `Ī*` (`NĪ*T`); with no mark the vowel keys and star are as they are, in steno order (`A*`, `*E`), and `EU` with the star is `I*`.

items: **Raw first.** Text that is exactly the raw notation of the keys it parses to is raw (`TPHAEPL`, `ORB`, `P-L`).

**Then short.** `+`, `~` and `#` anywhere (each once); the left hand up to the first vowel symbol, vowel key, star or `-`; the vowel part (marks, vowel keys, the star, at most one `-`, each key once, any order: `Ī*` and `*Ī` both read); then the right hand. Each part is read greedily, longest symbol first. So `NAEM` is `TPHAEPL`, `PL` is `PHR` (P and L), `FLĪT` is `TPHRAOEUT`.
**ASCII** where it reads no other keys: `SH` for `Š`, `CH` for `Č`, `ZH` for `Ž`, `NG` for `Ŋ`, `TH` for `Þ`, `OO` for `Ʊ` (`WISH` is `WEURB`, `BOOK` is `PWAOBG`).
**Then raw, leniently.** Anything else that parses as keys.
An outline written its own way is read back whole first; spaces around a `/` are ignored.

blocks.x: The same rules in `src/notation.rs` (lyk), `site/js/notation.js` (this site) and keymux's `steno/notation.rs`: `lyk lookup NAEM`, `lyk stroke flīt`, keymux's `steno lookup` and this site's Lookup all take either.

items: **lyk.** `lookup`/`keys`/`resolve` (lyk's column only, each group coloured by hand; dim for a solver read), `explain`, `quote`, `paths`, `family`, `ergonomics` (with the keys beside a short form), `mistakes` (the report; the tape is read in either form), `verify-lookup`, `build --report` and `solve --tape`. All through one function, `notation::outline`, reading `out/lyk/.keymux-notation.json` (before any build: the built-in rules' table, every stroke raw).
**This site.** Chips, tables, Lookup and the hover board's label (`data/notation.json`, the same table with its known outlines cut to the ones the site shows).

**keymux.** The tape (overlay and file), the live lookup, `{:outline:...}` and the keyboard diagram write and draw through the same file, which `deploy` ships beside the dictionaries; without it everything is Plover's notation. The diagram draws every key on its own unless the stroke's split is known; a known group lights as one block labelled with its symbol (`Ī` across the four thumb keys, `Š` over `-RB`), the star beside it.

**Stays raw** (read by programs): the dictionary files, typeladder's `lyk.codes.json`, the name lane files, the solver plugin, `mistakes --json` and `--drill`, `solve --misses`, the site's `data/` files and page sources.

blocks.x: A word the [solver](#/ref/fallback) reads is shown split as the solver read it: keymux asks the plugin's `groups` export right after a reading, and the plugin reads the run again with tracing on (each position in the beam keeps which reading of which stroke it came through), then reports, for each stroke, the chords of two keys or more and the vowel chord that wrote one sound. It costs nothing until keymux asks (the solver's own timing is unchanged: 2 ms a run on average, 6 ms at the 99th percentile), and a report about as much as one fresh reading (2-4 ms). A stroke the reading took whole (a known outline, a suffix chord) has no groups; a run with nothing close enough (the keys read back), a name, a lock or a late star reports nothing, and stays raw. `lyk solve OUTLINE` prints the groups.

`build` reads back every outline the rules wrote syllable by syllable from a word's sounds (59,946 outlines; a brief's keys say nothing about its sounds) and records, for each run of two keys or more, how its sounds split. Where the commonest split is not how the base symbols read the run, and at least 3 strokes split so, the run gets a group of its own (never one that is just its keys' own letters, and never a symbol another group of that hand already has). The outlines that split as the finished table reads them are listed as known (58,903); those that split another way are listed with their own form (316); 727 more whose own split does not read back as their keys (two sounds on one key, the `K` of `KWR` for k y) are not known and stay raw. The file is 1.37 MB. `lyk build --report` prints every run's splits and what each vowel and right-hand chord wrote.

Coverage: of 268,238 deployed outlines, 13,280 have a known split (10,998 of the 63,750 in `02-lyk-words.json`, where briefs and folded strokes are many); 45,937 backups have one. Everything else is raw.
